ov: Large birds of prey with huge hooked beaks and powerful talons. “Eagle” isn’t one natural group: it covers about 68 species big enough to hunt sizeable vertebrates.
wt: From 450 g (Great Nicobar serpent eagle) upward
rg: Mostly Eurasia and Africa. Only 14 species live elsewhere: 2 in North America, 9 in Central and South America, 3 in Australia.
df: Live prey such as mammals, birds, reptiles and fish, carried to a perch and torn apart with the beak.

cf.tip: Eagles and hawks belong to the same family. “Eagle” just marks the bigger species, large enough to hunt prey about 50 cm long or more.

fx: A bald eagle once flew carrying a 6.8 kg mule deer fawn, the heaviest verified load carried by any flying bird.
